gradients.name: window-bar
gradients.purpose: The --window-bar custom property: the overlay's and search view's window bars and setup's.

gradients.name: game-button
gradients.purpose: The game's bright blue window buttons: the overlay's toolbar and the search view's back button.

gradients.name: game-button-hover
gradients.purpose: A game-blue button under the pointer.

gradients.name: button-hover
gradients.purpose: Setup's primary button under the pointer, and held.

gradients.name: button-light
gradients.purpose: Setup's secondary buttons and the overlay's light icon and text buttons.

gradients.name: button-light-hover
gradients.purpose: A light-steel button under the pointer.

gradients.name: exp-fill
gradients.purpose: The game's EXP gauge lime: the Grind Tracker's EXP gauge fill, and nothing else.

gradients.name: exp-track
gradients.purpose: The light grey track under the EXP gauge's fill.

headline.purpose: The Map Name in Title Lettering on the title panel and setup's recognised test read; Time to Level and setup's step headings at the same size in plain ink. Held, the Time to Level figure and the rates drop to Light, never a fainter colour (the Best row's figure doesn't move, and stays bold); with no figure to give, the slot says why in 13px Light Panel Ink Steel, never a bare dash.

street.purpose: Above the Map Name in the same Title Lettering, the Mini Map's own idiom.

section-heading.purpose: Hidden Portals, Mobs and the Hunting Target's mob in Panel Ink: one step above the 13px bold rows they head.

status.purpose: The no-map status in the Map Name's slot, plain Panel Ink with no outline, so it doesn't read as a map name.

window-name.purpose: The window's name and the search view's title on the grey window bar; setup's step count.

title.purpose: Portal destinations, summary and rate values, the Hunting Target's figures and "You're here".

body-reading.purpose: Setup's prose and the search field: read at rest, one step larger than the overlay.

body.purpose: Overlay notes, the mob and rates tables, the suggestions; tabular figures.

body-small.purpose: Positions, labels, units, headers, the route, the arrival's trip, candidate rows, key hints and the footer.

label.purpose: Tags and the "Not sure" chip (uppercase only there).

shadows.name: window-inner-ring
shadows.purpose: Just inside the panel's frame; 0.65 on the title-marking hint.

shadows.name: bar-top-highlight
shadows.purpose: The top edge of setup's window bar; 0.6 on the doubt chip, 0.3 on setup's primary button, solid #fff on light steel.

shadows.name: game-button-bevel
shadows.purpose: The game's blue buttons; their white icon carries drop-shadow(0 1px 0 rgba(0, 50, 90, 0.45)).

shadows.name: pressed
shadows.purpose: A held game-blue button; deep steel uses inset 0 1px 3px rgba(10, 20, 50, 0.45), light steel the same at 0.25.

shadows.name: glyph-ring
shadows.purpose: The dark edge on mob dots, the you dot and the orange dots; the alert dot adds 0 0 0 2px #fff.

shadows.name: title-lettering
shadows.purpose: The --title-lettering text-shadow: a map's title only.

shadows.name: light-edge
shadows.purpose: A text-shadow on every line of text on the panel's body, so a busy scene can't swallow it.

tints.name: row-hover
tints.purpose: Edit Blue at 8%: suggestion and result rows under the pointer.

components.name: Grind Tracker Figures
components.description: The Session's figures set into the Grind Tracker's body on near-opaque Window Lavender: Time to Level with the light reset button at the far end, the rates as the panel's summary in miniature, then the share and deaths lines. The rates are Last 5 min, Session once it runs longer, and on a map with a Personal Best from its history the Best row, its light × in the percentages' column removing that best from the history. While Last 5 min beats the best over a full 5 minutes on the map, an 11px You Yellow star follows its period; its room is kept while it's off. Until the Session starts the box holds the Best row alone. Held (warming up, paused, or the EXP bar unread), the figures drop to Light, never fainter, all but the Best row's: it doesn't move.

narrative.northStar: The Window the Game Forgot to Ship
narrative.overview:
The overlay is one more of the game's windows laid over the screen, built from the two it sits beside. From the Mini Map it takes the light grey window bar with the window's name and small bright blue buttons, and the sky-blue title panel with the Street Name over the Map Name in light lettering outlined in blue. From the Quest Helper it takes the see-through periwinkle body with near-black text. The minimap's legend supplies the glyphs: blue portal rings, red mob dots, and the player's yellow dot. The pixel-art gold compass, the app icon, is the window's mark. The game supplies the materials and one signature move; organisation, hierarchy and density come from a working tool: EXP pace first when it is tracked, then hidden exits, then the mobs, then the way to the Hunting Target, then the credit. It is not a screenshot of a game window.

It is light because the game's windows are light, see-through because the game's windows over the screen are, and dense because it is read in glances between attacks. Every state is drawn in the same window. Doubt and problems get the game's orange, and nothing else does. The confirmed rejection is the generic dark dev-tools card with a stats table on top, which this world replaced. Setup is a window on the desktop rather than over the game: it keeps an opaque lavender body, navy ink and steel buttons under the same grey window bar, and shows a recognised map exactly as the overlay's title panel will. The title-marking window's hint is a small translucent lavender window.

Every window takes the pointer. The overlay is always clickable, but a click never takes the keyboard from the game except in the search view, where the query field needs it. The panel is dragged by its window bar or title panel when it sits inside the game or is detached, and resized by its sides or bottom corners, width only. Its buttons and setup's buttons carry the game's hover, pressed and keyboard-focus states; list rows in the search view take a faint hover tint. Its height follows its content. Nothing in any window moves but the world crawl's gauge: its fill eases to each new count, and a sheen runs along it while the crawl goes on. There is no other transition or animation anywhere: the Grind Tracker's EXP gauge changes with each reading, as the game's own does, without easing.
keyCharacteristics: The Mini Map's light grey window bar and sky-blue title panel over the Quest Helper's see-through periwinkle body, in a 4px-cornered frame.
Street Name over Map Name in light lettering outlined in blue, as the Mini Map draws its title.

Three icon vocabularies only: minimap glyphs (portal ring, mob dot, you dot and the you yellow star, mini-minimap) in CSS and SVG, drawn line icons on the game's small blue buttons, and the pixel-art compass as the window's mark.
Near-black ink with a faint light edge on the see-through body; navy ink on setup's opaque lavender.
Game orange appears only for doubt and problems.
NEXON's Maplestory typeface throughout, Light and Bold; numeric columns right-aligned.
Buttons in every window have the game's hover, pressed and focus states. No motion anywhere.

rules.name: The Orange Means Doubt Rule
rules.body: Game orange marks only uncertainty and problems: the "Not sure" chip, problem notes, the collapsed alert dot. A confirmed state never uses it, so orange can't become decoration. Search tiers are told apart by weight and ink, never by orange.

rules.name: The Minimap Legend Rule
rules.body: Portal blue, mob red and you yellow come from the minimap's legend and keep that meaning. Blue is for portals, red is for mobs and yellow is for where the player is, with no other uses but one: you yellow also draws the Grind Tracker's new-best star, since both are about the player.

rules.name: The EXP Lime Rule
rules.body: The lime of the game's EXP gauge draws the EXP bar's reading in the Grind Tracker and nothing else: not progress in general (the crawl gauge is Game Button Blue), and never a highlight.

rules.name: The Over the Game, See-Through Rule
rules.body: A window laid over the game is see-through: the overlay on the Quest Helper's glass, the title-marking hint on translucent Window Lavender. A window on the desktop (setup) is opaque. Same family, different footing.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Text on the see-through glass is the Quest Helper's near-black Panel Ink; text on lavender is navy Ink. Never mix them in one window.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: In the overlay all figures are tabular (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on the body), and numeric columns are right-aligned so EXP, HP, rates and share line up from one glance to the next.

rules.name: The Outlined Lettering Rule
rules.body: Only a map's title, the Street Name and the Map Name, uses the Mini Map's light lettering outlined in blue (the shared `--title-lettering` text-shadow: a 1px title-outline stroke in eight directions plus one soft 0 2px 1px drop). It appears on the overlay's title panel and in setup's recognised test read, nowhere else. Everything else, Time to Level included, is ink.

rules.name: The Notes Wrap, Names Truncate Rule
rules.body: Notes and the Map Name wrap so they can be read in full. Single-line facts (destinations, mob names, route stops, suggestion names, result maps) truncate with an ellipsis instead of growing the panel.

rules.name: The Chrome, Not Lift Rule
rules.body: Depth is drawn the way the game draws it, with highlights, bevels and hairlines. Nothing floats on a blurred drop shadow.

rules.name: The Light Edge Rule
rules.body: Text on the see-through glass keeps a faint light edge so a busy, saturated scene behind it can't swallow it. It is a legibility edge, as the Quest Helper's text has, not a glow: never coloured, never on the bars.

dos: **Do** build new overlay states from the game's window materials: the grey window bar, the Mini Map's sky-blue title panel, the Quest Helper's see-through glass with near-black text, and the game's bright blue buttons.
**Do** keep setup on its opaque lavender with navy ink and steel buttons under the same grey window bar.
**Do** use a see-through body for windows over the game and an opaque one for windows on the desktop.
**Do** reserve game orange for doubt and problems, and pair it with words and a shape (chip, dot, bordered note) so the state never relies on colour alone.

**Do** draw icons as minimap glyphs (portal ring, mob dot, you dot and the you yellow star, mini-minimap) in CSS or inline SVG, or as 2-stroke line icons on the game's small buttons; the pixel-art compass is the only raster and marks the window.
**Do** keep overlay figures tabular and numeric columns right-aligned.
**Do** let notes and the Map Name wrap, and truncate single-line facts with an ellipsis.
**Do** keep the Street Name above the Map Name wherever a map is shown as the overlay shows it.
**Do** draw the EXP bar's reading as the game's own EXP gauge, in EXP Lime, and nothing else in that lime.

**Do** give every button, in every window, hover, pressed and a 2px Edit Blue `:focus-visible` ring offset 2px: game blue on the overlay's window bars, light steel in its body, deep steel for setup's step forward and light steel beside it.
**Do** mark a selected row with Selection Periwinkle and its inset edge, and set a list into the body as an inset box.
donts: **Don't** return to the dark dev-tools card with a stats table on top.
**Don't** use orange, or the outlined title lettering, for anything other than their single roles.
**Don't** add small labels or kickers above content beyond the Street Name in the title panel; a label belongs only to the field or figure it names.
**Don't** let a click on the overlay take the keyboard from the game outside the search view.
**Don't** add motion (transitions or animations) to any window.
**Don't** float any window on a blurred drop shadow; depth is highlights, bevels and hairlines.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or icon fonts.
